title: Deep-learning design produced soluble analogues of membrane-protein folds with preserved binding functions
summary: A deep-learning pipeline based on inversion of AlphaFold2 and ProteinMPNN designed soluble proteins with claudin, rhomboid-protease and GPCR-like folds. Experiments reported stable, folded soluble designs and structural agreement with target folds. The researchers grafted functional motifs, including a ghrelin-receptor epitope that bound its antibody and active/inactive A2A-receptor-like designs that differed in mini-Gs binding; a binding-site knockout served as a control.
ai_technology: AF2seq deep-learning backbone design with ProteinMPNN sequence design
organization: École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne; University at Buffalo; University of Washington; Massachusetts Institute of Technology

evidence.tested: Experiments reported stable, folded soluble designs and structural agreement with target folds.
evidence.unknown: This is a protein-design proof of concept with in-vitro biophysical and binding assays; the analogues are not native membrane receptors and do not demonstrate signaling, drug activity or therapeutic efficacy. The GPCR analogues tested binding to mini-Gs in conformation-designed constructs. The separate live-catalog record on designed proteins modulating dopamine D1 receptor signaling reports a different binder/target and signaling result; this paper reports soluble receptor-fold analogues and binding assays, not D1 signaling modulation.
evidence.ai_role: The deep-learning design pipeline generated soluble analogues of complex membrane-protein folds and the scaffolds into which native functional motifs were grafted. The study tested solubility, thermal stability, structural accuracy and selected binding functions experimentally, including conformation-specific A2A-receptor-like constructs.
